system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Chicago, United States. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Chicago itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Chicago space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (West Town/West Loop, River North, Pilsen/Bridgeport, Logan Square/Wicker Park, Garfield Park, Hyde Park) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Chicago spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Chicago, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Rhona Hoffman Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1976; Chicago's benchmark for conceptual and socially engaged art, with Gordon Matta-Clark, Nathan Carter, Deana Lawson-era peers and decades of museum-caliber programming.

galleries.name: Kavi Gupta
galleries.address_hint: 835 W Washington Blvd and 219 N Elizabeth St
galleries.note: Chicago's most internationally visible dealer, representing Roger Brown estate, Jeffrey Gibson, Mickalene Thomas and Deborah Kass, with heavy global fair presence.

galleries.name: Gray (Richard Gray Gallery)
galleries.address_hint: 2044 W Carroll Ave (Gray Warehouse); 875 N Michigan Ave
galleries.note: Blue-chip house since 1963 bridging modern masters and living artists (McArthur Binion, Theaster Gates, Jaume Plensa), with a New York outpost and top-tier fair program.

galleries.name: Corbett vs. Dempsey
galleries.note: Scholarly recovery of Chicago Imagists and postwar abstraction alongside a sharp contemporary roster; a critical engine of the city's art history.

galleries.name: The Renaissance Society
galleries.note: Non-collecting kunsthalle founded 1915 that gave many artists their first US institutional show; still the city's most influential experimental exhibition program.

galleries.name: Mariane Ibrahim
galleries.note: Global platform for artists of the African diaspora (Amoako Boafo, Clotilde Jiménez); Chicago flagship with Paris and Mexico City spaces and major fair presence.

galleries.name: monique meloche gallery
galleries.note: Launched careers of Amy Sherald, Rashid Johnson and Ebony G. Patterson; consistently ahead of institutional taste since 2000.

galleries.name: Document
galleries.note: Rigorous photo- and lens-based program that has grown into one of the city's most critically respected younger galleries, with Lisbon expansion.

galleries.name: PATRON
galleries.note: Ambitious roster (Harold Mendez, Alex Chitty, Bethany Collins) and strong fair record; a leading voice among Chicago's second-generation dealers.

galleries.name: Western Exhibitions
galleries.note: Drawing-centric, Imagist-adjacent program since 2004 championing artists like Dutes Miller, Deb Sokolow and Sarah and Joseph Belknap.

galleries.name: Hyde Park Art Center
galleries.note: Founded 1939; the incubator that introduced the Hairy Who, and still the South Side's key exhibition, residency and teaching hub.

galleries.name: Arts Club of Chicago
galleries.note: Since 1916 a private club with a public, non-collecting gallery of consistently first-rate international contemporary exhibitions.

galleries.name: Volume Gallery
galleries.note: Nationally significant platform for American collectible design and art-design crossovers; regular at Design Miami and EXPO Chicago.

galleries.name: Andrew Rafacz Gallery
galleries.note: Long-running West Town gallery with a crisp painting-and-object program and steady support of mid-career Chicago artists.

galleries.name: Shane Campbell Gallery
galleries.note: Influential dealer since 1999 who brought a national conceptual/painting roster to Chicago and helped shape the current gallery generation.

galleries.name: Aspect/Ratio
galleries.note: Video, new media and time-based work; one of the few Chicago dealers built around moving image, with an active fair presence.

galleries.name: Goldfinch
galleries.note: Artist-focused gallery pairing emerging Midwest talent with overlooked older women artists; anchor of the Albany/Garfield Park corridor.

galleries.name: Devening Projects
galleries.note: Artist-run since 2007, with an international abstraction network and exchanges with European project spaces.

galleries.name: Regards
galleries.note: Small, sharply curated gallery known for idiosyncratic emerging and re-discovered artists and outsized critical attention.

galleries.name: Secrist | Beach
galleries.note: Successor to Carrie Secrist Gallery (est. 1991), continuing a contemporary painting and sculpture program with national reach.

galleries.name: Gallery 400
galleries.note: UIC's free kunsthalle: research-driven, politically engaged exhibitions that have long incubated Chicago's curatorial talent.

galleries.name: Logan Center Exhibitions
galleries.note: University of Chicago's contemporary exhibition program, commissioning ambitious projects with strong South Side and international ties.

galleries.name: Wrightwood 659
galleries.note: Tadao Ando–designed non-collecting exhibition house for socially engaged art and architecture; among the city's most talked-about venues.

galleries.name: Graham Foundation
galleries.note: Grant-making body whose galleries stage internationally important architecture and art exhibitions and publications.

galleries.name: Chicago Cultural Center
galleries.note: City-run, free, non-collecting galleries; home base of the Chicago Architecture Biennial and large survey shows of local artists.

galleries.name: Rebuild Foundation / Stony Island Arts Bank
galleries.note: Theaster Gates's archive, residency and exhibition complex; a globally cited model for art-led neighborhood work.

galleries.name: Arts + Public Life / Arts Incubator
galleries.note: University of Chicago residency and gallery on the South Side, launching artists through commissions and community programs.

galleries.name: South Side Community Art Center
galleries.note: Founded 1940 and dedicated by Eleanor Roosevelt; the oldest African American art center in the US, now a National Historic Landmark with active contemporary shows.

galleries.name: Carl Hammer Gallery
galleries.note: Since 1979 the definitive dealer for self-taught and outsider art (Henry Darger, Lee Godie) alongside contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Zolla/Lieberman Gallery
galleries.note: The gallery that founded the River North district in 1976; enduring program of contemporary painting and sculpture.

galleries.name: Catherine Edelman Gallery
galleries.note: Leading Midwest photography dealer since 1987, mixing established names with its Chicago Project emerging-artist platform.

galleries.name: Stephen Daiter Gallery
galleries.note: Authority on 20th-century documentary and avant-garde photography, including the Chicago Institute of Design legacy, plus contemporary work.

galleries.name: Threewalls
galleries.note: Since 2003 a key alternative space and residency, now focused on artist-led, community-rooted commissions and publications.

galleries.name: Roots & Culture
galleries.note: Long-running noncommercial space giving early exhibitions to emerging Chicago and national artists.

galleries.name: Chicago Artists Coalition
galleries.note: HATCH and BOLT residencies plus exhibitions; a career-launching pipeline for emerging Chicago artists and curators since 1974.

galleries.name: Weinberg/Newton Gallery
galleries.note: Non-commercial gallery pairing artists with social-justice organizations on issue-driven exhibitions.

galleries.name: Heaven Gallery
galleries.note: Loft-scale artist-run mainstay since 2000 blending visual art, music and performance in Wicker Park.

galleries.name: Julius Caesar
galleries.note: Cooperative artist-run space whose alumni and exhibitors populate Chicago's commercial galleries; a bellwether of the scene.

galleries.name: The Franklin
galleries.note: Backyard open-air pavilion run by Edra Soto and Dan Sullivan; a beloved, widely covered artist-run venue.

galleries.name: Comfort Station
galleries.note: Tiny landmarked hut with an outsized multidisciplinary program of exhibitions, film and music.

galleries.name: Iceberg Projects
galleries.note: Daniel Berger's backyard gallery known for queer histories, HIV/AIDS-related art and museum-quality small shows.

galleries.name: Roman Susan
galleries.note: Storefront and public-facing projects sustaining experimental practice on the far North Side.

galleries.name: 6018North
galleries.note: House-museum-style site for immersive installation and social practice, with high-profile citywide collaborations.

galleries.name: LVL3
galleries.note: Artist-run gallery and widely read online artist interview series; a hub for emerging practices.

galleries.name: Engage Projects
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery with a strong emphasis on abstraction and international emerging artists.

galleries.name: Linda Warren Projects
galleries.note: Two decades of representing Chicago-based painters and sculptors, with a track record of nurturing mid-career artists.

galleries.name: moniker gallery
galleries.note: West Loop gallery bridging contemporary painting with street- and design-influenced practices; strong collector following.

galleries.name: Vertical Gallery
galleries.note: Chicago's leading urban/street-art gallery, showing internationally known muralists and printmakers.

galleries.name: Woman Made Gallery
galleries.note: Founded 1992 to exhibit women and nonbinary artists; a long-standing feminist institution with juried national shows.

galleries.name: Co-Prosperity
galleries.note: Public Media Institute's experimental hall; anchor of Bridgeport's DIY scene and Version Fest.

galleries.name: Zhou B Art Center
galleries.note: Large studio and exhibition complex with international exchange programs; a magnet for Bridgeport's monthly openings.

galleries.name: Mana Contemporary Chicago
galleries.note: Vast studio-and-gallery building housing project spaces, residencies and exhibitions in Pilsen.

galleries.name: Tiger Strikes Asteroid Chicago
galleries.note: Chicago chapter of the national artist-run network, curating peer-to-peer exhibitions with strong critical visibility.

galleries.name: Chicago Art Department
galleries.note: Artist-run gallery, studios and education platform central to Pilsen's contemporary scene.

galleries.name: Rootwork Gallery
galleries.note: Curator-led space centering Black and Brown artists and healing-based, community-rooted exhibitions.

galleries.name: Produce Model Gallery
galleries.note: Young, well-reviewed gallery giving early solo shows to emerging Chicago and national artists.

galleries.name: ACRE Projects
galleries.note: Exhibition arm of the ACRE residency, showing alumni and expanding the city's emerging-artist network.

galleries.name: Pilsen Outpost
galleries.note: Latinx-focused storefront gallery and shop, deeply tied to Pilsen's mural and print traditions.

galleries.name: Uri-Eichen Gallery
galleries.note: Politically engaged Pilsen space pairing activist history with contemporary art.

galleries.name: 4th Ward Project Space
galleries.note: Artist-run storefront bringing rigorous abstraction and conceptual work to the South Side.

galleries.name: Hyde Park Kunstverein
galleries.note: Small membership-driven kunstverein staging research-based exhibitions, talks and publications.

galleries.name: Blanc Gallery
galleries.address_hint: 4445 S Dr Martin Luther King Jr Dr
galleries.note: Bronzeville gallery and performance venue showcasing contemporary Black artists.

galleries.name: Gallery Guichard
galleries.note: Long-running commercial gallery of the African diaspora, anchoring the Bronzeville Artists Lofts.

galleries.name: Bridgeport Art Center
galleries.note: Converted warehouse with studios and multiple exhibition floors; major node in the South Side gallery circuit.

galleries.name: Project Onward
galleries.note: Studio and gallery for artists with disabilities, with a nationally recognized roster and fair presence.

galleries.name: Arts of Life (Circle Contemporary)
galleries.note: Studio collective for artists with disabilities whose Circle Contemporary gallery has gained real critical traction.

galleries.name: Filter Photo
galleries.note: Photography nonprofit with year-round exhibitions and an annual festival that draws national curators.

galleries.name: Ukrainian Institute of Modern Art
galleries.note: Since 1971 a Ukrainian Village fixture presenting modern and contemporary exhibitions well beyond its diaspora remit.

galleries.name: Ed Paschke Art Center
galleries.note: Free Northwest Side center devoted to the Imagist painter's legacy plus rotating contemporary shows.

galleries.name: Epiphany Center for the Arts
galleries.note: Restored church complex with multiple galleries programming contemporary and community-based exhibitions.

galleries.name: Hairpin Arts Center
galleries.note: Community-run gallery in the landmark Hairpin Lofts, central to Logan Square's arts programming.

galleries.name: Galerie F
galleries.note: Poster, print and street-art gallery that helped drive Chicago's mural boom.

galleries.name: Chicago Truborn
galleries.note: Gallery devoted to Chicago street and graffiti artists, with active public-mural commissioning.

galleries.name: Elephant Room Gallery
galleries.note: Emerging-artist gallery near Columbia College, known for accessible group shows and first solos.

galleries.name: Color Club
galleries.note: Artist-run gallery, studios and event space fostering Northwest Side experimental work.

galleries.name: PO Box Collective
galleries.note: Community art space combining exhibitions, craft and activism on the far North Side.

galleries.name: Lawrence & Clark
galleries.note: Apartment-scale gallery with a quietly influential program of Chicago conceptual and object-based art.

galleries.name: Chicago Manual Style
galleries.note: Artist-run space known for tightly curated, often humorous exhibitions of emerging Midwest artists.

galleries.name: Printworks Gallery
galleries.note: Works-on-paper specialist since 1980, a steady presence for contemporary printmaking and drawing.

galleries.name: Jean Albano Gallery
galleries.note: River North veteran since 1985 showing contemporary painting, assemblage and pop-inflected work.

galleries.name: Maya Polsky Gallery
galleries.note: Longstanding dealer with a strong Eastern European and Russian émigré contemporary program.

galleries.name: Gallery Victor Armendariz
galleries.note: Contemporary figurative painting and sculpture with a national collector base.

galleries.name: Addington Gallery
galleries.note: River North gallery of contemporary painting and mixed media, active for over two decades.

galleries.name: Gruen Galleries
galleries.note: One of the district's oldest dealers, showing contemporary painting and sculpture since the 1970s.

galleries.name: Hilton Asmus Contemporary
galleries.note: International contemporary and photography program with an ambitious cross-disciplinary exhibition schedule.

galleries.name: Ken Saunders Gallery
galleries.note: Successor to Marx-Saunders and a leading US dealer in contemporary studio glass.

galleries.name: Alan Koppel Gallery
galleries.note: Modern and contemporary art shown alongside 20th-century design; a discreet but respected dealership.

galleries.name: Richard Norton Gallery
galleries.note: Specialist in historic Chicago modernism whose scholarship underpins the market for the city's mid-century artists.

galleries.name: Thomas McCormick Gallery
galleries.note: Postwar American abstraction and contemporary painting; instrumental in reviving interest in mid-century Chicago artists.

galleries.name: Douglas Dawson Gallery
galleries.note: Ancient and non-Western material presented in dialogue with contemporary sculpture; a distinctive, long-established program.

galleries.name: Fulton Street Collective
galleries.note: Studio building and gallery hosting monthly open studios, jazz and large group exhibitions.

galleries.name: Glass Curtain Gallery, Columbia College Chicago
galleries.note: Columbia's flagship public gallery, presenting curated contemporary shows and student-faculty projects.

galleries.name: Ralph Arnold Gallery, Loyola University
galleries.note: Loyola's contemporary gallery, named for the Chicago collagist, with a socially engaged exhibition program.

galleries.name: Chicago Printmakers Collaborative
galleries.note: Print studio and gallery since 1989 sustaining Chicago's deep printmaking culture.

galleries.name: Beverly Arts Center
galleries.note: Far South Side multidisciplinary center whose galleries serve a region otherwise underserved by contemporary art venues.
